ops.text: Decoders engineered for real-time hardware operation sit below this value: the Kittiwake decoding core, run on a cluster of FPGA cards, crosses at $p_{\mathrm{thr}}\approx 0.00598$ under the same uniform circuit-level model [⟦new.A6⟧]. Inserted into Eq. (1) together with the MWPM value $p_{\mathrm{thr}}^{\mathrm{SC,cl}}\approx 0.0075$, this lower threshold multiplies the LER at $d=7$ and equal $p$ by $(0.0075/0.00598)^{4}\approx 2.47$, an illustration of how a modest loss of threshold is amplified by the code distance.

Dedicated streaming hardware such as the Kittiwake core [⟦new.A6⟧] already completes window-based decoding within a microsecond-scale cycle, which sets the bar for a hardware implementation of the network.
